releaseNotes: check:secrets stopped accusing security docs of leaking credentials. The credential-extraction scan matched the command names awk, grep and sed with no word boundaries, so `sed` matched inside ordinary prose — closed, exposed, compromised, used, parsed — and any line that later said `credentials` was reported as an extraction snippet. A launched business hit this on a dated incident record whose only offence was the phrase 'fail-closed guard | PASS — anonymous credentials'. The gate was failing exactly the documents it exists to protect, and the only ways out were editing shared tooling or doctoring an incident record to satisfy a bad regex. Both are worse than the warning.

The pattern is now \b-anchored on both sides. The leading boundary kills the prose family; the trailing one rules out awkward and grepping. Real snippets still warn: the fixture pair proves an incident write-up full of closed/exposed/compromised near 'credentials' stays silent while `VAR=$(awk -F= ... /path/to/file.env)` in committed markdown still fires. Two of the three warnings this gate was raising against the skill's own playbook were this same false positive.

The boundaries cut both ways, and review caught the half that was missing: anchoring also excludes prefixed executables, so gawk, mawk, nawk, gsed, ggrep and the compression wrappers zgrep, bzgrep and xzgrep — which the unanchored form had only ever caught as substrings, by accident — would have gone silent while extracting the same raw values. The command list is now enumerated: ripgrep, [gmn]?awk, g?sed, (zstd|bz|xz|lz|z)?[efg]?grep, rg. Alternation order is load-bearing because JS matches leftmost-first, not longest, so ripgrep precedes the grep branch and zstd precedes z. One fixture per variant, twenty of them, so the enumeration cannot rot back to the three bare names.

Enumeration is deliberate rather than lazy, and the code comment now says so, because the obvious generalisation is actively wrong. A prefix wildcard such as [a-z]*(grep|awk|sed) reintroduces this gate original bug verbatim: English words END in these tokens — closed, exposed and parsed for sed; squawk and mohawk for awk. Only an explicit command list separates the executables from the prose, so the near-miss fixture pins awkward, grepping, squawk, mohawk, org and rgb alongside the incident-prose fixture.

Four founder-facing pages are now rendered from the documents they were always supposed to mirror, and the drift this fixes was not cosmetic. security-review.html was missing about ten of the fifteen sections its own opening line claimed to cover, including authentication and authorization, backend and API controls, revenue abuse, and accepted risks. store-console.html had lost the console click-path table, the Apple pre-submission compliance row covering PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy, ATT and account deletion, and the entire seven-item App Review Information checklist, which is Guideline 2.1 rejection-risk content. onboarding.html labelled a card Personalization and filled it with Attribution content, and had dropped the push permission prime step altogether. orchestration.html was missing seven sections and carried a state-integration table row that was never real data.

check:generated-pages is the new gate, and it asserts three things because any one alone passes vacuously: every page at the root of business/ is declared in scripts/lib/artifact-pages.ts, every declared page exists, and every page written from Markdown byte-matches a fresh render. A declare-and-verify shape was considered and rejected. Hashing a file proves someone touched it, not that the HTML is right, and it would have grandfathered all four content bugs behind a green gate.

scripts/lib/markdown-lite.ts is a hand-rolled parser for the subset these documents actually use: headings to H3, one status line, tables, flat lists, one ordered list, bold, inline code, one fenced block. It throws on anything else rather than degrading to a paragraph, because a parser that silently renders an unsupported construct as something else is the exact failure this gate exists to catch. No markdown dependency was added: two package.json files held in parity, plus dependabot splitting dependency-group updates by root, makes each half of a split update land red.

design.html and analytics-plan.html are declared starter placeholders and are deliberately not generated. Their real content only exists after a launch produces it, so rendering them from a plan document would present a plan as a finished result. Filename symmetry makes generating all eight look right; it is not.

SECURITY.md, STORE_CONSOLE.md and ONBOARDING.md gave up six pieces of internal vocabulary that check:founder-copy bans on the pages they now render into. The hand-authored HTML had already been translating them silently, which is part of how the drift went unnoticed: the page said Release Checks while the document said Release Proof. The document now says what the founder reads, and check:security's required phrase moved with it.

One accepted downgrade: orchestration.html loses its three-chip status dashboard. Synthesizing those labels needs per-page logic bolted onto a generic renderer. The trade is slightly less glanceable in exchange for seven restored sections and the removal of fabricated content.
